SignOutCleaner still wipes the unchanged prefix tailoring.request.; account switch in RemoteSignInGateway.signIn also runs cleaner.clear() + wipeAll(). Cross-account reuse is harmless anyway: apps-backend looks up (userId, requestId).

New runId -> new key -> new requestId (aNewRunIdSendsANewRequestId, aNewRunIdDoesNotReuseTheRequestIdOfAnUnfinishedRun). The second test pins a money regression for abandoned unfinished runs; see finding 1.

RemoteResumeTailor.kt:52-60: SUCCEEDED returns without clearing; a non-SUCCEEDED finished job clears then throws; the catch clears only non-RESUMABLE AiExceptions; cancellation and non-AiException errors keep the id. successKeepsThePendingIdAndFailedClearsIt fails on base. Re-keyed assertions in RemoteResumeTailorFailureTest/RemoteResumeTailorTest/RemoteResumeTailorRequestIdTest keep the same null/non-null expectations. Backend (revamp/be-all, which the v2 client targets): start() returns the existing (user, requestId) row with 200 before reserveCredit; finish() calls spendTailoringCredit only on RUNNING->SUCCEEDED; FAILED and INTERRUPTED never spend, so a fresh requestId after FAILED charges once on success. The PR body cites apps-backend main (v1 allowance claim/markUsed, schema still has section and no answer); the conclusion holds on be-all too.

runId: String? = null in TailoredResume, TailoredResumeDto and both mappers; JSON TEXT column, no Room schema change; legacy JSON decodes to null (TailoredResumeRunIdJsonTest via the real JsonConverters). Runner stamps tailored.copy(runId) in the same upsert as the result; AcceptChanges/UpdateBulletDecision/HandEdit use copy() so the marker survives. TailoringRunnerRunIdTest covers skip with an empty ledger, the stamp, one SPEND across two skips, and a new runId re-tailoring. runId is a UUID, no PII. A stale result from an earlier runId never satisfies the skip for a new tap.

Demo: restoredAfterFinish..., reTailor...NewRun..., crashAfterResultBeforeSpend... and retryAfterFailure... pass with only the fake's signature changed. crashAfterResultBeforeSpend now takes the skip path (stored runId) and still ends with one SPEND and the stored result; its 'Reruns' name is now loose but the assertions hold. Process death traced at every point: before the call (pending id may exist unsent; resend creates one job), after server debit before store (same requestId, 200, no debit), after store before SPEND (skip + one SPEND in demo, no-op in prod), after SPEND (skip). No free run: storedForThisRun is only true after a SUCCEEDED (server-charged) result or an offline result whose SPEND the skip records.

findings.rule: Issue #322 / D58 'no second charge for one tap'; base behaviour kept the pending requestId per application until the job finished, so an abandoned unfinished job was resumed by the next tap
findings.trigger: Prod, balance 2. Tap Tailor (r1). Server job J1 starts (202 RUNNING, credit reserved). Either the user swipes the app away during the multi-minute job (task removed, so the next launch starts a fresh back stack and no TailoringNavKey(r1) is restored), or polling hits a network drop and the user taps Go back on Tailor failed. They open the job again and tap Tailor (navigateToTailoring, wired by #277): new runId r2, so idFor(r2) mints a new requestId and the server starts J2. J1 finishes SUCCEEDED and spendTailoringCredit charges 1; J2 charges 1 more. The user paid 2 credits for one visible result, and J1's result is unreachable because tailoring.request.r1 has no navigation key left. With balance 1, reserveCredit counts J1 as reserved, so r2 gets 402 NO_CREDIT; J1 then spends the last credit and its result is never shown. On base (key tailoring.request.app-1, kept on cancellation and resumable failures), r2 resent J1's requestId and received J1's result with one charge. aNewRunIdDoesNotReuseTheRequestIdOfAnUnfinishedRun pins this regression. A 'stuck' id cannot block later runs: be-all reconcileInterrupted turns a stale RUNNING row into FAILED INTERRUPTED, and the client clears the id on FAILED.
findings.title: A new tap after an abandoned, unfinished run starts a second server job, so one result can cost two credits
findings.proof: RemoteResumeTailorRunIdTest: backend.reply(202, tailoringBody("RUNNING")); backend.fail(502, "AI_PROVIDER_ERROR") (poll drop, Unavailable, resumable); runCatching { tailorOverStore().tailor(candidate, job, gap, "app-1", null, "run-1") }; succeed(); tailorOverStore().tailor(candidate, job, gap, "app-1", null, "run-2"); assert that the run-2 start carries run-1's requestId. This fails at head. Fix: keep a per-application pointer under the same prefix, for example tailoring.request.unfinished.<applicationId>. Write it with the minted id. When a new runId has no key of its own, adopt the pointer's id. Clear the pointer on SUCCEEDED, FAILED and non-resumable failures. A new tap after a finished run still gets a new requestId, so c2 holds.

findings.rule: Review checklist 5 / D64: an edited test must keep its assertion meaningful under an honest name
findings.trigger: aFinishedJobForgetsItsRequestId now passes run-1 then run-2, so it passes whether or not a finished job forgets its id. At head the code does the opposite of the name: SUCCEEDED keeps the id (successKeepsThePendingIdAndFailedClearsIt). Restore the per-run clear-on-success behaviour and this test still passes. The test now duplicates aNewRunIdSendsANewRequestId under a name that states the old, defective behaviour. The PR body defers the rename to a follow-up.
